item.title: City of Milwaukee next municipality to sue fire truck makers over alleged price fixing scheme
item.description: The City of Milwaukee has filed a class action lawsuit against major fire truck manufacturers, alleging a price-fixing scheme.

item.title: Brewers and manager Pat Murphy agree to contract extension
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers announced today that they have reached an agreement with manager Pat Murphy on a multi-year contract extension. Terms of the deal were not announced. But according to reports, the deal extends Murphy’s contract through the 2028 season with a team option for 2029. “Pat Murphy has been an incredible partner and leader […]

item.title: Snap-on returns as title sponsor for IndyCar weekend at Milwaukee Mile
item.description: Kenosha-based tool manufacturer Snap-on Inc. will again serve as the title sponsor for this year’s IndyCar Weekend at the Milwaukee Mile racetrack at Wisconsin State Fair Park in West Allis. The event, to be called the 2026 Snap-on IndyCar Weekend at Milwaukee Mile, will be held on Aug. 28-30. This year’s event will be expanded […]

item.title: Concordia University launches master’s degree program in AI
item.description: Concordia University Wisconsin in Mequon has launched an online master’s degree program in artificial intelligence, the university announced Thursday.

item.title: Wisconsin Frontier Technology Consortium launches with $950,000 WEDC grant
item.description: The Wisconsin Technology Council is leading a new statewide Frontier Technology Consortium backed by a $950,000 WEDC grant.

item.title: Harambee neighborhood jazz café to close
item.description: After nearly five years in business, Sam’s Place Jazz Café in Milwaukee’s Harambee neighborhood will close today. item.title: Business organization leaders react to Supreme Court’s ruling against Trump tariffs
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court struck down many of President Trump’s sweeping tariffs Friday, prompting mixed reactions from Wisconsin business leaders.
